 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 24.01.2012 passed in MVC.No.7625/2010 by the learned VII Additional Judge, Member, MACT, (SCCH-3),
Bengaluru, seeking for enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts of the case are that, on 10.07.2010, at about 5.30 p.m., the claimant was riding the Motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-04-Y-3452 in Honnenahalli Village, C.B.Pura Taluk from East to West direction.
At that time, a car bearing registration No.KA-04-B-1849 came from Bagepalli side with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the claimant's motorcycle.
Due to this impact, the claimant sustained grievous injuries.
Heard the arguments from both sides and perused the records.

4. The Tribunal has awarded compensation under various heads as follows:

In the present case, from the evidence on record, it is proved that the claimant has suffered fracture NC: 2023:KHC:21427 of both bones of left leg, head injury and other grievous injuries all over the body.

6. Considering the nature of the injuries sustained, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head 'pain and sufferings' at Rs.50,000/- and towards 'loss of amenities and future unhappiness' at 50,000/- are found to be correct.
Therefore, the same remains in tact.
7. The Tribunal has granted only Rs.3,992/- under the head 'medical expenses incurred' as the claimant was able to produce bills and receipts to that extent only.

But considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the claimant as discussed above and that the claimant was in patient for a period of 10 days in hospital and undergone surgery, even in the absence of sufficient bills and receipts to consider the fact that the claimant was admitted in the hospital for a period of ten days and undergone surgery, I deem it appropriate to award Rs.10,000/- under the head 'medical expenses'.

Accordingly, compensation of Rs.10,000/- under the head 'medical expenses' is NC:
2023:KHC:21427 granted.
Further, the compensation awarded under the head 'incidental expenses like nourishment, attendant and conveyance' is found to be on lower side.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.15,000/- is awarded under the head 'nourishment, attendant and conveyance'.
8.

The Tribunal has erred in assessing the notional income of the claimant at Rs.4,000/- per month,
which is on the lesser side.
The accident was occurred in the year 2010.
Therefore, the notional income would be Rs.5,500/- per month as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
9. The claimant is not able to attend his work as coolie atleast for a period of four months.
Accordingly, compensation of Rs.22,000/- (Rs.5,500X4) is awarded under the head 'loss of income during laid up period'.
The notional income taken by the Tribunal at Rs.4,000/- p.m., is on the lower side as discussed above.

Therefore, NC: 2023:KHC:21427 notional income of Rs.5,500/- p.m.,
may be taken as income of the claimant.
10. The doctor has stated that the claimant has suffered 50% permanent disability in respect of left lower limb and whole body disability is assessed at 17%.
The Tribunal has assessed 20% as functional disability, which is just and proper.
Therefore, the Tribunal is correct in holding the disability at 20% and that is confirmed herein.

12. Accordingly, compensation of Rs.2,77,200/- is awarded under the head 'loss of future income due to disability'.
13. The Tribunal upon discussing on Issue No.1 regarding negligence held that the claimant had contributed 25% negligence and the car driver had contributed 75% negligence.
The entire charge sheet is filed against the driver of the car.
Therefore, as per the investigation officer, it is informed that the car driver was completely rash and negligent in driving the car and caused the accident.
Admittedly, the car was moving from Bagepalli to C.B.Pura.
The place of the incident is NH-7 and near the accident spot, to go to Honnenahalli, besides national highway, there is a service road and to reach the service road, there is an underpass.
There is a road to go to Honnenahalli from the accident spot at the distance of half furlong.

Therefore, the left side of the National NC:
2023:KHC:21427 Highway is leading from C.B.Pura to Bagepalli and the right side of the road is leading from Bagepalli to C.B.Pura.
The place of accident is shown as National Highway from C.B.Pura to Bagepalli.
Therefore, the movement of vehicle should be from C.B.Pura to Bagepalli.
But the car was coming from Bagepalli to C.B.Pura.
Therefore, the driver of the car was driving the car on the wrong side of the road.
Towards western side, the National Highway is going from Bagepalli to C.B.Pura.
Therefore, the car driver ought to have maintained his car on left side of the road from Bagepalli to C.B.Pura.
But the car driver has taken the car on the wrong side of the road from Bagepalli to C.B.Pura and in this way, the accident was caused.
Therefore, the driver of the car drove the car towards wrong side of the road and caused the accident.
Therefore, this shows the car driver was completely rash and negligent in driving the car.

Taking the car that too on National Highway where there is divider on the middle of the road, clearly demarcating the movement of vehicle NC:
2023:KHC:21427 and taking the car on the wrong road itself is rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the car.
Therefore, in this regard, the Tribunal has committed an error in fastening contributory negligence at 25% on the claimant.
Therefore, it is proved that the driver of the car was completely rash and negligent in driving the car and caused the accident.
Therefore, the finding on Issue No.1 is modified by holding that the driver of the car was completely rash and negligent in driving the car and 100% liability is fastened on him.
Therefore, the contributory negligence at the ratio of 25% fastened on the claimant, i.e., the driver of the motor cycle is set aside.
14. The Tribunal has granted compensation of Rs.25,000/- towards 'loss of expectation of life'.
This amount is double claim.
Since the claimant is granted compensation for 'loss of future income due to disability'.
Therefore, the said quantum is set aside.

The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.3,09,992/-, but the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.3,99,200/-.

Therefore, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.89,208/-
(Rs.3,09,992 - Rs.3,99,200) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:21427 realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
17.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed-in-part.

ii. The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.7625/2010 dated 24.01.2012, is hereby modified holding the claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.89,208/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
iii. The appellant/claimant is not entitled for the interest for the delayed period of 48 days in filing the appeal.

iv. Costs made easy.
 v. Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy of the order forthwith without any delay.

vi. Draw award accordingly.
